CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old female with past medical history of congestive heart failure, kidney stones, and prior colonoscopy presents for evaluation of low hemoglobin. Patient reports experiencing fatigue and dizziness over the past couple of months, becoming tired with activities such as walking a mile or going to work that she previously tolerated without difficulty. She denies weight loss, loss of appetite, or syncope. Regarding hemochezia, she denies current blood in stools; however, she did have blood in stools approximately three years ago which prompted a colonoscopy showing mild diverticulosis with no subsequent issues. She denies dark, tarry, or black stools. She denies heavy menstrual bleeding. Regarding her congestive heart failure, she has recently struggled with salt intake compliance while traveling to Vermont, including a stop at McDonald's for fast food. She has noticed some swelling in her legs but denies it being extreme. She denies shortness of breath or orthopnea. Regarding her kidney stones (which she had a couple of years ago), she denies recent flare-ups, back pain, flank pain, or hematuria. She reports mild nasal congestion due to seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for fatigue, dizziness, and nasal congestion related to seasonal allergies. Negative for weight loss, loss of appetite, syncope, hemochezia, melena, heavy menstrual bleeding, shortness of breath, orthopnea, back pain, flank pain, hematuria, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, kidney stones, diverticulosis.

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 milligrams daily, Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily, Lasix 40 milligrams once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently traveled to Vermont. Has struggled with salt intake compliance, including consumption of fast food during travel.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are stable with normal blood pressure and heart rate. Cardiac exam reveals a three out of six systolic ejection murmur, previously noted. Lower extremities show trace to one plus pitting edema in both ankles.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from approximately six months ago shows left ventricular ejection fraction of approximately 45% and moderate mitral regurgitation. Hemoglobin is 8.2 (low).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Anemia: Laboratories including anemia profile to be sent to determine type of anemia. Patient referred to gastroenterology for further evaluation with likely endoscopy and colonoscopy.
Congestive heart failure: Patient is retaining fluid. Starting Lasix 40 milligrams once daily. Continuing Toprol 50 milligrams daily and Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Patient instructed to monitor salt intake, weigh herself daily, and contact physician if weight increases as additional diuretic may be needed.
Kidney stones: Currently stable. Patient advised to continue monitoring diet and staying hydrated and to call with any questions.
